learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Given points with integer coordinates, return the **maximum number of points that lie on one straight line**. Points may repeat.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Can points repeat? (Yes — a duplicate is on every line through its twin.)
- Coordinate range? (Large — products overflow int, and doubles are not exact.)
- n up to a few thousand — is O(n²) fine? (Yes.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: Every line through a fixed point is identified by its direction. Store the direction as dy/dx reduced by the gcd with a fixed sign, and equal directions hash equal exactly — no floating-point comparisons.

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Slopes as double: points far apart with nearly equal slopes compare equal.
- Vertical lines (dx = 0) dividing by zero.
- Forgetting duplicate points.
- Two sign conventions for the same direction: (1,2) and (-1,-2).

learn.title: 17 · Reference solution

designClaim: for each point, group every other point by the exact slope to it, stored as a reduced integer pair with one sign convention, plus a count of duplicates — O(n²) time, and no floating point
customTemplate:
int[][] P(params int[] xy) => Enumerable.Range(0, xy.Length / 2).Select(i => new[] { xy[2 * i], xy[2 * i + 1] }).ToArray();
return MaxPoints.OnALine(P(1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3));
